title: procurement-tools bill of materials
description: A shopping list expressed as requirements rather than products. Written as YAML (bom.yaml). Lines start described-but-unidentified and acquire a part number as research settles them; a line is quotable at either stage, which is what lets an RFQ go out before the choice is made.

purpose.description: What the assembled set is for. Suppliers quote better against a stated purpose, and it is what lets them propose a substitution that actually works.

destination.description: Address profile id, matching addresses.yaml used by price-scan.

id.description: Stable and never reused, so a supplier quoting against revision 2 can still be matched to revision 4.

description.description: Vendor-neutral description of what the line has to be. Written so a supplier who has never seen the spec can quote it.

spec_ref.description: Spec id, optionally with a variant and requirement ids: 'laser-measure-2026-08', 'laser-measure-2026-08@budget', or 'laser-measure-2026-08@budget#REQ-001,REQ-004'. The @variant part is required whenever the spec has variants, since the same line can be justified by different requirements under each.

identified.description: Present once a specific product has been chosen for this line. Absent means the line is still a requirement, which is a legitimate state to send to a supplier.

substitution.description: allowed = supplier may propose anything meeting the description. equivalent-only = must meet every referenced requirement. none = this exact part number, usually because it has to interoperate with something already owned.

target_price.description: Per-unit. Carried into the RFQ only when the user opts in — it anchors the supplier.

criticality.description: contingent = only needed if another line resolves a particular way; say which in notes.

groups.description: Optional grouping of lines by subsystem or by which supplier is likely to carry them. A group is the natural unit of one RFQ.
